'''Mohammad Ataul Karim''' ({{langx|bn|মোহাম্মদ আতাউল করিম}}; born 4 May 1953) is a [[Bangladeshi American]] scientist and higher education administrator, with expertise in electro-optical systems, optical computing, and pattern recognition. Ataul Karim is ranked amongst the top 50 researchers who contributed most to journal ''[[Applied Optics]]'' in its 50-year history.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.odu.edu/ao/news/index.php?todo=details&id=32201 |title=News at Old Dominion University |publisher=Odu.edu |date=2012-06-06 |access-date=2013-10-12 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121214223455/http://www.odu.edu/ao/news/index.php?todo=details&id=32201 |archive-date=14 December 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.opticsinfobase.org/ao/journal/ao/anniversary/50mostpublished.cfm |title=Applied Optics - 50 Most Published Authors |publisher=Optics InfoBase |date= |access-date=2013-10-12}}</ref> Ataul Karim served as provost, executive vice chancellor and chief operating officer <ref>{{cite web |url=http://pbn.com/UMass-Dartmouth-appoints-new-provost,88446 |title=UMass Dartmouth appoints new provost - Providence Business News |publisher=Pbn.com |date=7 May 2013 |access-date=2013-10-12}}</ref><ref name="autogenerated1">{{cite web |url=http://staging.theinstitute.ieee.org/people/achievements/achievements-june-2013 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130811142307/http://staging.theinstitute.ieee.org/people/achievements/achievements-june-2013 |url-status=dead |archive-date=11 August 2013 |title=Achievements: June 2013 - IEEE - The Institute |publisher=[[IEEE]] |date=2013-06-07 |access-date=2013-10-12}}</ref><ref name="opnmagazine-digital48">{{cite web |url=http://www.opnmagazine-digital.com/opn/july_august_2013?pg=48#pg48 |title=Optics & Photonics News - July/ August 2013 |publisher=Opnmagazine-digital.com |date=2013-06-17 |access-date=2013-10-12}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=UMass Dartmouth launching honors college this fall |url=https://www.tauntongazette.com/news/20190808/umass-dartmouth-launching-honors-college-this-fall |work=Taunton Daily Gazette |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210711225957/https://www.tauntongazette.com/news/20190808/umass-dartmouth-launching-honors-college-this-fall |archive-date=2021-07-11}}</ref> of the [[University of Massachusetts Dartmouth]] between June 2013 – 2020, and was for 9 years the first vice president for research<ref>{{cite web |url=http://blue.odu.edu/ao/ia/insideodu/20130509/topstory5.php |title=Karim Stepping Down to Accept Provost Position at UMass Dartmouth |date=9 May 2013 |work=InsideODU |publisher=Old Dominion University |access-date=2013-10-12 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131014120008/http://blue.odu.edu/ao/ia/insideodu/20130509/topstory5.php |archive-date=14 October 2013 |df=dmy-all}}</ref> of [[Old Dominion University]] (ODU) in [[Norfolk, Virginia]].

==Biography==
Mohammad Ataul Karim was born in [[Barlekha]], a border town in [[South Sylhet]]. He attended Shatma Primary for his elementary education and Patharia Chotolekha High for a year after which he left home to be schooled at [[Faujdarhat Cadet College]] (1965–1969), Sylhet [[MC College]] (1969–1972), and the [[University of Dhaka|University of Dacca]] (1972–1976) wherefrom he received his bachelor's honors degree in physics. Ataul Karim earned his master's degrees in physics (1978) and electrical engineering (1979), and a doctor of philosophy degree in electrical engineering (1982) from the [[University of Alabama]].<ref name="umassd.edu">{{Cite web |url=http://www.umassd.edu/provost/people/mohammadkarim/ |title=Mohammad Karim - UMass Dartmouth |access-date=27 December 2013 |archive-date=28 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131228030645/http://www.umassd.edu/provost/people/mohammadkarim/ |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Ataul Karim practiced creative writing in high school. Many of his popular science writings in [[Bengali language|Bengali]] appeared in ''Biggyan Shamoeeki'' and ''Bangla Academy Biggyan Patrika'' during 1972–1976. Of these, the most significant were ''Biborthon Kahinee'', a series of articles on cosmic and biological evolution, and ''Shamproteek'', a monthly feature on current affairs in science, both of which appeared in ''Biggyan Shamoeeki''. By the second year of his bachelor's degree in 1974, he had completed his first book manuscript, which he submitted to [[Bangla Academy (Bangladesh)|Bangla Academy]] for publication. After about two years, the academy informed him that it was not prepared to take a chance on its juvenile author. This episode troubled him deeply, ending his creative writing efforts in Bengali. All his subsequent books and articles were written in English, and all were published from outside of Bangladesh.{{citation needed|date=August 2019}}

A 2004 government of Bangladesh report<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://publications.iom.int/bookstore/free/Diaspora_Linkage_Bangladeshis.pdf |title=Institutionalising Diaspora Linkage: The Emigrant Bangladeshis in UK and USA |access-date=27 December 2013 |archive-date=27 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131227110656/http://publications.iom.int/bookstore/free/Diaspora_Linkage_Bangladeshis.pdf |url-status=dead}}</ref> and a number of books in Bengali, including ''Bangladesher Shera Bigyani'' (Hitler A. Halim, ''Shikor'', 2004), ''Medhabi Manusher Golpo'' ([[Mohammad Kaykobad]], ''Annyaprokash'', 2005), "Medhabi O Binoyi Manusher Golpo" (Mohammad Kaykobad, "Shore O", 2020), and "Tarae Tarae Khochito" (Fardin Munir and Munir Hasan, "Odomya Prokash", 2022)  as well as ''Star Insight'', cite him as an example of the outstanding success of the Bangladeshi diaspora.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://archive.thedailystar.net/starinsight/2011/07/01/cover.htm |title=Dr. Mohammad Ataul Karim: Beyond Excellence in Physics |work=Star Insight |publisher=The Daily Star |date=4 June 2011 |access-date=21 October 2011}}</ref> His efforts to correct illegal practices that otherwise discriminated against international graduate students were featured by the [[Chronicle of Higher Education]],<ref>{{cite web |last=Wilson |first=Robin |url=http://chronicle.com/article/A-University-Uses-Quotas-to/9731/ |title=A University Uses Quotas to Limit and Diversify Its Foreign Enrollments - Faculty - The Chronicle of Higher Education |publisher=Chronicle.com |date=1999-05-14 |access-date=2013-10-12}}</ref> ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' in "Hidden Costs of a Brain Gain"<ref>{{cite news |author= |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB983409306676287048 |title=Hidden Costs of a Brain Gain |work=The Wall Street Journal |date=March 2001 |access-date=2013-10-12}}</ref> and in turn by David Heenan in his book "Flight Capital: The Alarming Exodus of America's Best And Brightest".

==Professional affiliations==
Prior to University of Massachusetts Dartmouth (2013–present), he had held academic appointments with the [[University of Arkansas at Little Rock]] (1982–1983), [[Wichita State University]] (1983–1986), [[University of Dayton]] (1986-1998: founding director, Electro-Optics Program, 1990–1998; chair of electrical and computer engineering, 1994–1998), [[University of Tennessee at Knoxville]] (1998–2000: head of the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering), [[City College of New York]] of the [[City University of New York]] (2000–2004: dean of engineering), and [[Old Dominion University]] (2004-2013: vice president for research). Ataul Karim is an elected fellow of seven societies: [[Optical Society of America]] (1993), [[Society of Photo-Optical Instrumentation Engineers]] (1995), [[Bangladesh Academy of Sciences]] (2002), [[Institute of Physics]] (2006), [[Institution of Engineering & Technology]] (2006), [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] (2009), and Asia-Pacific Artificial Intelligence Association (2022).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://aaia-ai.org/fellows?words=Mohammad%20Karim |title=Asia-Pacific Artificial Intelligence Association}}</ref>

==Scholarly research==
He supervised MS/PhD research of over 60 graduate students<ref name="umassd.edu"/> and authored 19 books, 13 book chapters, and over 365 research papers.<ref name="umassd.edu"/> He guest-edited 36 journal special issues in areas of communication, computing, multimedia, networks, optics, pattern recognition, infrared systems, remote sensing, and software.

==Relevance to Bangladesh==
He leads the [[International Conference on Computer and Information Technology]], now in its 25th year.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.iccit.org.bd/2013/ |title=ICCIT — ICCIT 2013 |publisher=Iccit.org.bd |date=2013-07-31 |access-date=2013-10-12}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://archive.thedailystar.net/campus/2009/01/02/camspotlight.htm |title=ICCIT 2008 Redefining ICT Future in Bangladesh |author=Jamil-ur-Rob |newspaper=The Daily Star |date=11 January 2009 |access-date=20 January 2018}}</ref> Since 2009, with assistance of 5 teams of guest editors, Ataul Karim produced 20 journal special issues that featured works of  Bangladesh-based researchers in the fields of communications,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://ojs.academypublisher.com/index.php/jcm/issue/archive |title=Archives |publisher=Ojs.academypublisher.com |date= |access-date=2013-10-12}}</ref> computing,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://ojs.academypublisher.com/index.php/jcp/issue/archive |title=Archives |publisher=Ojs.academypublisher.com |date= |access-date=2013-10-12}}</ref> multimedia,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://ojs.academypublisher.com/index.php/jmm/issue/archive |title=Archives |publisher=Ojs.academypublisher.com |date= |access-date=2013-10-12}}</ref> networks,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://ojs.academypublisher.com/index.php/jnw/issue/archive |title=Archives |publisher=Ojs.academypublisher.com |date= |access-date=2013-10-12}}</ref> and software.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://ojs.academypublisher.com/index.php/jsw/issue/archive |title=Archives |publisher=Ojs.academypublisher.com |date= |access-date=2013-10-12}}</ref> His edited book on "Technical Challenges and Design Issues in Bangla Language Processing"
<ref>{{cite book |url=http://www.igi-global.com/book/technical-challenges-design-issues-bangla/72370 |title=Technical Challenges and Design Issues in Bangla Language Processing (9781466639706): M. A. Karim, M. Kaykobad, M. Murshed: Books |year=2013 |publisher=IGI Global |isbn=9781466639706 |access-date=2013-10-12}}</ref> provides a state-of-the-art platform for information communication technology research and development that is of significance to nearly 260 million Bengali-speaking people who live in Bangladesh, India and in diaspora in the Middle East, Europe, and the US. This milestone work includes 16 chapters coauthored by 41 researchers from [[Bangladesh]], [[Canada]], [[India]], [[Ireland]], [[Norway]], the [[United Kingdom|UK]], and the [[United States|US]].

Ataul Karim is known for his advocacy and writings <ref>{{Cite news |url=https://opinion.bdnews24.com/2011/12/24/dhaka-university-can-it-turn-around/ |title=Dhaka University: Can it turn around? &#124; the Opinion Pages |date=24 December 2011}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/opinion/education/news/dhaka-university-challenges-the-future-1727953 |title=Dhaka University: Challenges for the future |date=11 April 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/opinion/views/news/remaking-the-universities-bangladesh-the-case-trash-journals-3082001 |title=Remaking the Universities in Bangladesh: The Case of Trash Journals |date=28 July 2022}}</ref> to improve ranking of universities in Bangladesh, and for containing questionable journal publication and faculty recruitment practices. He serves on the board of trustees and/or advisory boards of a number of private universities including [[Ahsanullah University of Science and Technology]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.aust.edu/administration/board_of_trustees |title=Board of Trustees}}</ref> [[North South University]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.northsouth.edu/about/int-ab.html |title=International Advisory Board (IAB) &#124; North South University}}</ref> and [[Metropolitan University, Sylhet]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://metrouni.edu.bd/about-us/leadership-and-management/board-advisers/ |title=Advisors &#124; Metropolitan University}}</ref> and the Board of Regents of the North American Bangladeshi Islamic Community,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://nabic.org/about-us/ |title=About Us – North American Bangladeshi Islamic Community}}</ref> known for its many projects in education, environment, healthcare, poverty alleviation, and relief and rehabilitation.
